# User-Defined Functions

- same difference in the syntax
  - The first line has ()
  - The lines of the function body are in {}

## 1) Example 1: No Output Values

```{r}
odd_even = function(input1) {
  if(input1%%2 == 0) {
    print("Even")
  } else { #actually can have else start a line in a function but don't write it like that bruh
    print("Odd")
  }
}
```

## 2) Example 2: Output Values

```{r}
# Same keyword as Python - return 

# Important differences with the return line:
  # Use () with return
  # In R, you can return ONLY ONE variable/object as output
    # What do to if we want to return multiple vars?  
    # Put them together in an R DATA STRUCTURE and return the structure as one variable

my_func = function(a,b,c) {
  out1 = a*b^2
  out2=b-a
  return (list(out1, out2)) # gotta return one object
}
```

- Other than these points/differences, everything else is the same as Python user-defined functions:
  - Input order and stating input names: my_function(in2=4, in1=5, 6)
  - Default values: my_function = function(in1, in2, in3=5)
  - You can create a function without any inputs/outputs
  - Seeing a return line stops a function from running, so all the lines under that return line would be skipped.
  - Same idea as Python about global and local variables.
    - Global vars are seen inside the function body.
    - Local vars are NOT seen outside the function body.
    - If a local var has the same name as a global var, it overwrites ONLY inside the function body.
